topic: DeepSeek capped its free chat: run the open weights locally instead
thesis: DeepSeek capped its free chat because its compute ran short, but the weights it already open-sourced run on your gaming PC tonight with no quota, no key and no bill.
explanation_path: Open on the thing that changed: between November 15 and 16, 2026, the free app and website began refusing work they used to do -- long conversations inactive for more than seven days could no longer be resumed, single prompts were capped at around 40,000 Chinese characters, and a usage-limit notice appeared when the day's quota ran out, for some accounts in less than two hours of continuous chatting. Establish why before any fix: the notices blame insufficient computing capacity, and the load is record-setting -- 59.2 trillion tokens in one week on this exact model, first in the world -- so waiting it out or paying is not currently an option; there is no paid consumer tier, and the API that serves the same model is billed per token. Then the reframe: DeepSeek also gives its models away as weights, MIT-licensed, and has for a long time -- the 671B R1 plus six distills from 1.5B to 70B. Land the consequence on the viewer's hardware: a GGUF at Q4_K_M is 8.99 GB for the 14B distill and 19.9 GB for the 32B, sizes a 16 or 24 GB gaming PC already handles, loadable tonight in LM Studio or with a single Ollama command. Close honest: a distill is a student of the big model, not the big model -- and the current chat model's own open weights are a 552B-backbone project no gaming PC is running this week.

claims.claim: Between November 15 and 16, 2026, DeepSeek's free app and web chat began enforcing usage caps: long conversations inactive for more than seven days could no longer be resumed, single prompts were capped at around 40,000 Chinese characters, and a usage-limit message appeared at the daily quota.
claims.source_title: DeepSeek users report chat limits as the service cites capacity constraints

claims.claim: Product notifications blamed insufficient computing capacity, some users hit the daily-quota notice after less than two hours of continuous chatting, and DeepSeek currently offers no paid option for the consumer app.
claims.source_title: Yicai: DeepSeek starts limiting free usage

claims.claim: In the week of November 9 to 15, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 handled 59.2万亿 tokens (59.2 trillion tokens), the most of any model globally according to OpenRouter data cited by Yicai.
claims.source_title: Yicai: DeepSeek starts limiting free usage

claims.claim: The model behind the official web and app chat is DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, served on the API as deepseek-flash with a 1M-token context.
On the paid API, that same model bills $0.15 per 1M input tokens (cache miss, off-peak) and $0.6 per 1M output tokens (off-peak), with peak rates double.
DeepSeek publishes open weights: the R1 model card lists DeepSeek-R1 at 671B total and 37B activated parameters with 128K context, plus six distilled checkpoints from 1.5B to 70B, under MIT license.
The DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B GGUF downloads 8.99 GB at Q4_K_M (7.92 GB at Q3_K_L) and supports 128k context.
The 32B distill GGUF downloads 19.9 GB at Q4_K_M (17.2 GB at Q3_K_L), the realistic ceiling for a 24 GB machine.
Ollama ships the same distills as one-command pulls with a 128K context window: deepseek-r1:7b is 4.7GB, deepseek-r1:14b is 9.0GB, deepseek-r1:32b is 20GB.
LM Studio's own guidance: with 16GB of RAM you can run the 7B or 8B distills; the full 671B model needs roughly 192GB or more.
claims.source_title: DeepSeek R1: open source reasoning model, LM Studio Blog

analogy_candidates.vehicle: All-you-can-eat buffet installing a ticket machine while giving away the cookbook
analogy_candidates.mapping: the hosted chat is the restaurant, someone else's GPUs with portions rationed when the kitchen overheats; the open weights are the cookbook plus your own stove (the gaming PC), where nobody counts your plates
analogy_candidates.limit: a cookbook copies for free and cooks identically, while a 9 GB distill is a real download that cooks a smaller menu than the 671B chef, and your stove size caps which recipes fit at all

analogy_candidates.vehicle: Gym installing a turnstile vs taking the barbell home
analogy_candidates.mapping: the cap is the gym limiting visits during a capacity crunch; the weights are the barbell you take home and lift whenever you like
analogy_candidates.limit: a barbell taken home lifts exactly the same as the gym's, but a local distill is a lighter barbell than the one the hosted chat uses

misconceptions.myth: DeepSeek started charging everyone or broke entirely.
misconceptions.reality: The free chat got caps whose notices cite insufficient computing capacity, and as of November 17 no paid consumer tier exists to remove them (claims 1, 2).

misconceptions.myth: If the chat is capped, DeepSeek is off the table.
misconceptions.reality: The R1 weights and its six distills are MIT-licensed downloads that run unmetered on your own GPU (claims 6, 7, 9).

misconceptions.myth: Running DeepSeek locally means running the same model you chatted with.
misconceptions.reality: On 16 to 24 GB you run a 14B or 32B distill trained to imitate R1, not the 671B original, which needs roughly 192GB+ of RAM (claims 6, 10).

glossary.definition: A single packaged file of model weights that runtimes like LM Studio, Ollama and llama.cpp load directly.
Shrinking weights to about 4 bits each to cut file size and memory use, at a small accuracy cost.
A smaller open model (Qwen or Llama) fine-tuned on a big model's outputs to imitate it at a fraction of the size.
DeepSeek's server-side allowance of free chat turns, enforced per account and shown as a usage-limit message.

unverified: Whether the caps apply identically to every account; reports vary and DeepSeek has published no unified rules.
The exact daily message count; no fetched page states one, only per-account reset times.
A 72-hour inactivity cutoff some users described, alongside the seven-day notices.
Tokens per second for the 14B or 32B distill on a 16-24 GB gaming GPU; this needs our own measurement before the script cites a speed.
Press speculation that a paid consumer subscription is coming, based on Coding Plan strings reportedly found in the web front-end; nothing official.
suggested_outline:
Open on the notice: usage limit reached, old chats locked after more than seven days inactive, inputs capped around 40,000 Chinese characters -- and no paid tier to escape it.
Explain the squeeze: record load of 59.2万亿 tokens in a week against insufficient computing capacity, and the per-token API is the only official way to pay ($0.15 in, $0.6 out per 1M, off-peak).
Land the move: the weights are already free -- 8.99 GB for the 14B distill, 19.9 GB for the 32B, one command in Ollama or a search in LM Studio -- and be honest that a distill is the student, not the 671B teacher.
notes: No DeepSeek page states the caps. The official API change log's latest entry (2026-11-13) covers the new application APIs and an open-source demo chat client that imports your exported chat history -- but that client runs on the paid API, so continuing a rescued conversation bills per token. Conflict on the inactivity cutoff: seven-day notices (TechNode, Yicai) versus 72-hour user reports (Yicai); treat both as reported, not universal. The current chat model's own weights are open (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 552B backbone parameters, 8B activated per token during prefill and 16B during decode), but the model card states the release does not include a Jinja-format chat template and points to a local inference folder for weight conversion -- not a tonight project, which is why the distills carry the how-to. Thin spots: no first-party tokens-per-second on consumer GPUs, and the exact quota mechanics are unpublished. Trust Yicai and TechNode over aggregator rewrites for the event details; both are dated, bylined, and cite the product notifications.
viewer_situation: You use DeepSeek's free app or website for long chats, this week it started telling you the usage limit was reached, and the gaming PC next to you has 16 to 24 GB of memory doing nothing about it.
process_steps: Install LM Studio from lmstudio.ai (or Ollama from ollama.com) on the gaming PC.
Search the model catalog for DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B GGUF.
Pick Q4_K_M: 8.99 GB fits 16 GB; pick the 32B at 19.9 GB if you have 24 GB.
Download, load the model in the chat tab, and ask away with no quota and no API key.
Or open a terminal and run ollama run deepseek-r1:14b (9.0GB).
objection: A 14B distill is not the 671B DeepSeek you were talking to, and the current chat model's own open weights (V4.1-Flash, 552B backbone parameters) are nowhere near a gaming PC -- local means a smaller student model, and nobody has measured its speed on my card.
